generatedProse.concept-context: A psychology report follows a recognisable shape, often the structure of a journal article. The introduction sets out the question and the theory behind it. The method explains how the study was run, in enough detail that another psychologist could repeat it. The results report what was found, with the statistics but without interpretation. The discussion weighs what the findings mean and how far they answer the question.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two psychology students write up the same small study, and we look at how each handles the parts.

Tom opens by giving away the main finding, mixes an explanation of how participants were tested into the results, and adds his own opinion where the results should simply report the data. The pieces are all there, but they are in the wrong places, so a reader cannot follow the study from question to answer. The structure is working against him.

Amara lets each part do its own job. The introduction poses the question, the method explains how the study was run, the results report the data without comment, and the discussion weighs what they mean. A reader can follow the thread from start to finish. The structure is doing the work.

Both wrote up the same study. Only Amara placed each piece in the part that reports it.
generatedProse.summary: A psychology report has a recognisable shape: introduction, method, results and discussion, each doing its own job. Together they carry a reader from the question, through how the study was run, to what was found and what it means. You can now recognise the parts and tell which one a piece of writing belongs to. With what research is, how a study is shaped, and the shape it takes, you have a map of research in psychology.

check.body: In the worked example, what made Amara's write-up easier to follow than Tom's?

items.text: Each part did its own job: the question in the introduction, then the method, the results, and their meaning.
It was written in more formal, academic language.
It gave the main finding away in the introduction.
It included her own opinion in the results.

feedback.correct: That's right. Amara let each part do its own job, so the reader could follow the study from question to answer.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what Amara did with the parts, rather than the style of the writing.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara's write-up was clearer because each part did its own job. Formality, giving the finding away early, or opinion in the results do not help the reader follow the thread.
